task1.title: Destination and salaries of Anthropology graduates
task1.prompt: The chart below shows what Anthropology graduates from one university did after finishing their undergraduate degree course. The table shows the salaries of the anthropologists in work after five years.

visuals.caption: Destination of Anthropology graduates (from one university)
Salaries of Antrhpology graduates (after 5 years' work)

chartDesc.overview: Just over half of anthropology graduates entered full-time work after graduation, and after five years of employment, the majority in all sectors earned $75,000 or more.
keyFeatures: From the pie chart, full-time work was the most common post-graduation destination at 52%, followed by part-time work (15%) and unemployment (12%).
From the pie chart, the smallest group was part-time work combined with postgraduate study (5%), while full-time postgraduate study and not known accounted for 8% each.
From the table, government sector employees had the highest percentage earning $100,000+ at 50%, compared to 40% of freelance consultants and 30% of those in private companies.

From the table, the lowest salary bracket ($25,000–49,999) contained the smallest proportion of graduates in all employment types (5% for freelance consultants and government sector, and 10% for private companies).

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

task2.title: Telling children they can achieve anything if they try hard enough
task2.prompt:
In some cultures, children are often told that they can achieve anything if they try hard enough.

What are the advantages and disadvantages of giving children this message?
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
